answer: Agents join small surety rings: each member posts a bond that covers the whole ring, and if any member is proven fake, every bond in the ring is slashed. An honest haven therefore costs a forger dearly, because each pearl of a fake identity needs real co-signers willing to risk their own stake, and honest agents refuse rings with strangers, so a Sybil operator must either pay many honest members or watch its rings collapse inward.
